<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object), list_datasets (literal, a string literal in PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE), query_dataset (literal, a string literal in PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `98753142b1efa0b55309a42243f4afcd3c1731de` — the merge of head `13eaec9ec63d27db69ea42ce4ada9555019a8cc9` into base `1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 98753142b1efa0b55309a42243f4afcd3c1731de && git checkout 98753142b1efa0b55309a42243f4afcd3c1731de
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 13eaec9ec63d27db69ea42ce4ada9555019a8cc9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 && git merge --no-ff 13eaec9ec63d27db69ea42ce4ada9555019a8cc9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `13eaec9ec63d27db69ea42ce4ada9555019a8cc9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.test.ts

Read for this record: card #33733 (body and all four comments: triage 6891883794, re-lane 6892365476, claim 6892496349, dev report 6893391372), the PR body, the 14-file list, the net diff against merge base `a557fa38`, and the check-runs on this head. The seat also had me read the Rulings section of its order; no judgment below rests on it. The 11 `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` hunks and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT; they are read here for ② and for the registry header's own label rule.

**Check-runs at review time: 13 success, 10 skipped, 21 in progress, 0 failed.** Build Core, Test Core 1-8, the Type Check and Lint families and Live E2E UI had not answered. The gate verdicts are therefore not in; this PASS is the contract reading only, and landing waits on those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Registry.** Two members join `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai']`, in sorted position (`get_record` · `list_datasets` · `query_data` · `query_dataset` · `query_records`). `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedToolName` derive from the map, so nothing else in the file owes an edit. Both names are snake_case, sit in no second group and do not start with `action_`. Right.
- **Spelling.** The names equal `LIST_DATASETS_TOOL_NAME` / `QUERY_DATASET_TOOL_NAME` in `packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`, and the new pin imports those constants, so the registry cannot drift from the ADR-0149 D2 spelling. Right.
- **Readers, each read on this head:**
  - `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts:145` builds its universe from the registry: a skill naming either tool stops drawing the warning-severity `ai-skill-tool-unresolved`. Intended.
  - `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:503` (`worldAnnotation`): a bridged tool of either name now gets `openWorldHint: false`. That is true of both (they read this environment's own datasets) and equals what MCP's native registration asserts.
  - `PLATFORM_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` / `PLATFORM_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL_NAMES` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts:311`, `:323`): **the dev's reading is verified.** The docblock calls the sets deliberately partial. Both pins are subset-only: one bridges the registry and asserts every annotated name is in it, the other iterates the two sets and asserts each name is in the registry. Neither asserts that a registry reader is in the read-only set, so no pin reds. A bridged pair gets no `readOnlyHint`, which reads as the protocol's cautious default. `query_data`, `search_knowledge` and `visualize_data` are in the same position on `main`.
  - Name collision: where the native MCP dataset tools are registered, `bridgeTools` skips the bridged namesake (`nativeToolNames`, #31836), so the pair is never registered twice.
  - `ChatbotEnhanced.answerSource-31868.test.tsx:225` and `mapMessages.persistedChart-25908.test.ts:112` assert containment of other names only. `build-progress.zod.ts`, `skill.zod.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`, `bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `toolResultParsers.ts` and `check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` name the registry in prose only.
- **Generated artifacts needed no change: verified by reading.** `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` list the export names, not the values. A grep for sibling members (`search_package_docs`, `remove_sample_data`) finds no generated file, reference doc or second hand copy of the list.
- **Labels.** All 11 built-in packs (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant) gain both keys inside the `chatbot.tool` block, in sorted position. Each value is a sentence in the pack's language; none equals the tool id or the title-caser's output; no English is copied into another pack. zh-Hant is in Traditional characters (檢視指標 / 按指標查詢). The header's second duty is met.
- **Not verifiable from here:** that cloud `service-ai` registers the pair (cloud PR #4557). It is carried from the card. ADR-0149 D2 and its D7 row 5 say the same in this repo, and a wrong group fails cloud's conformance test at the pin bump.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds. The declared type does not move; the published runtime value widens, and two published consumers change their answer on it (the lint universe and the MCP world hint). Nothing is removed.
- `@object-ui/i18n: patch` holds: its packs ship and gain keys only.
- **`Metadata-protocol: added` and `@objectstack/spec: minor` — nit N1, see ④.** The same kind of edit landed three days ago as `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` (#32668, contract review 6836202589, which rejected `added` on the code: `skill.tools[]` parses any string before and after, and the registry feeds only a warning-severity lint finding). By AGENTS.md checklist step 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The declaration here is internally consistent (`added` takes at least `minor`) and over-declares; it does not under-declare. It changes nothing that ships: 26 pending changesets already take `@objectstack/spec` to `minor` in its fixed group, and the release notes place the entry under 新增能力 on either reading.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope observation 1 (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` MCP tool table omits the dataset pair): predates the card and concerns MCP, not this registry. No action owed by this PR.
- Out-of-scope observation 2 (`PLATFORM_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` unchanged): answered in ①. Leave as is; the reader does not demand it and omission is the cautious direction. This matches the answer given on #32668.
- File surface: held. `packages/mcp` is untouched; the locale edits are the two keys per pack; none of #33734's files is in the diff.
- For the seat: N1 leaves two records with opposite readings of the same edit (6836202589: `none`; this PR: `added`). One standing reading should be named so the next registry card does not re-decide it.

### ④ Design judgment

`platform-tool-names.ts` holds against the code it cites: `../../ai/dataset-tools.zod` resolves, declares both names and shapes, and `registerDatasetTools` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` registers the pair. `platform-tool-names.test.ts` agrees with the contract: the pin reads the group, both membership answers and a `query_datasets` control, and the dev's ablation showed it red without the names.

- **N1 — nit.** `Metadata-protocol: added` / spec `minor` against the `none` / `patch` reading of #32668 (②). No effect on what ships. Accept as a deviation, or correct the line in a later prose-only edit; a changeset edit now would move the head.
- **N2 — nit.** The `service-ai` docblock is looser than the schema it points at. (a) `list_datasets` returns the datasets the caller may query, with their dimensions and measures and the term matches, not "the installed datasets and the metrics each defines": a dataset the caller is not admitted to is absent, and dimensions are listed too. (b) `query_dataset` runs a selection against ONE saved dataset and may name several measures, so "through one governed metric" understates it. (c) In "declared once in `../../ai/dataset-tools.zod` (ADR-0149 D2), which MCP registers too", MCP registers the tools, not the file. None of this misleads a reader about the registry's contract; the wording follows the card.
- **N3 — nit.** The changeset names the lint effect but not the MCP effect (`openWorldHint: false` for a bridged tool of either name). The PR body names it.
- Observation, outside ④ (lane seat's ACCEPT): the de label `Über eine Kennzahl abfragen` has no object and reads less naturally than its neighbours (`Die benötigten Daten abfragen`). It is still a German sentence and passes the rule.

0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 3 nits.
